newsitem.title: USA: Leslie-ADM pegs US corn 8.89 bln bu, soy 2.24 bln.
newsitem.headline: Leslie-ADM pegs US corn 8.89 bln bu, soy 2.24 bln.

text.p: The Conrad Leslie-ADM Elevator survey on Friday estimated U.S. corn production based on Sept 1 conditions at 8,889,508,000 bushels and soybeans at 2,244,760,000 bushels versus 8,976,715,000 bu of corn and 2,242,417,000 bu of soybeans Leslie estimated last month.
The estimates are based on inquiries with 1,200 grain elevators in the Corn Belt.

The estimates compare with U.S. Agriculture Department's Aug 1 estimates of 8,694,628,000 bu for corn and 2,299,675,000 bu for soybeans. U.S. corn production in 1995 totaled 7,373,876,000 bu and soybeans 2,151,834,000 bu.
U.S. average production for the past five years has been 8,152,954,000 bu corn and 2,143,000,000 bu soybeans.
Leslie pegged average corn yield at 121.3 bushels per acre, against last month's USDA estimate of 118.7 bu, the five-year average of 118.6 bu and last year's 113.5 bu.
"The corn crop is late," Leslie said, adding topsoil mositure was short throughout the Corn Belt as of Sept 1.
Leslie pegged end-season carryout on Sept 1, 1997, at 709 million bu against 374 million bu a year earlier, based on current demand estimates by USDA.
Leslie estimated average soybean yield at 35.4 bu an acre versus last month's USDA estimate of 36.2 bu, the five-year average of 36.1 bu and last year's 34.9 bu.
Leslie pegged end-year carryover stocks at 115 million bu on Sept 1, 1997, compared to 170 million bu a year earlier, based on USDA demand projections.

Leslie said soybean crop development is also late this year, with Illinois still yet to set 13 percent of its pods as of September 1 compareds with the usual 2 percent. No leaves were yet dropping in Illinois versus the usual 7 percent.
Leslie noted the average date of the first autumn freeze (32 degrees Fahrenheit) was Oct 1 on a line down to and across the lower third of Minnesota, Wisconsin and Michigan.
He said the Oct 15 freeze line lies along the southern Iowa border below the northern 40 percent of Illinois, the northern 75 percent of Indiana and then down to the southern Ohio border.
